findings.title: Dashboard query loads up to 5,500 documents in a single round trip
findings.why_it_matters: Convex functions have document-read and output-size limits. Fetching 1,000 deals + 500 activities + 2,000 posted invoices + 2,000 month invoices in Promise.all will exceed those limits for medium workspaces, causing the dashboard to fail outright. Even before limits, serializing and transferring that payload adds latency on mobile networks.
evidence: All four queries run in Promise.all and results are filtered/aggregated in the function
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the four broad takes with aggregate queries: openDealsCount via count, overdueActivitiesCount via filtered count, overdueInvoicesTotal and revenueMTD via sum/aggregate helpers. Keep only small recent/overdue lists (already sliced to top-5) and load them from separate, explicitly limited queries.

findings.title: AuthProvider value object changes on every useSession poll, triggering downstream re-renders
findings.why_it_matters: Better Auth's useSession may re-validate periodically, returning a new data object even when the session is unchanged. AuthProvider's useMemo rebuilds the entire AuthContextValue (including callback references) on every data change because signInEmail, signOut, and clearError are not memoized with stable dependencies and the value object is recreated. Every context consumer re-renders on each poll.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/providers/auth-provider.tsx:134 useMemo depends on [state.status, state.error, data, signInEmail, signOut, clearError]
signInEmail, signOut, clearError are created with useCallback but included as useMemo deps, so identity changes propagate
No selector or split context prevents every consumer from re-rendering
findings.suggested_fix: Split context into status/error/user/session and action contexts, or memoize the value object more carefully so that unchanged sessions do not recreate the context value. Consider using useMemo on individual callbacks with stable dependency arrays.

findings.title: Invoice detail and lists render inside ScrollView without virtualization
findings.why_it_matters: Invoice and activity lists use ScrollView with .map over all queried rows. For orgs with many invoices, this mounts every row component upfront, allocates images/text nodes for the entire list, and blocks the JS thread during initial render. FlatList would recycle views and improve scroll performance materially.
evidence: No FlatList, FlashList, or windowing is used
findings.suggested_fix: Replace ScrollView-based lists with FlatList (or @shopify/flash-list) for invoice and activity screens, providing keyExtractor and getItemLayout where possible.

findings.title: App ships placeholder PNG icon and splash assets likely not optimized
findings.why_it_matters: The icon.png, splash.png, and adaptive-icon.png in the diff are binary placeholders. Large unoptimized PNGs increase the app bundle size and APK/IPA download size. On mobile, every megabyte affects store conversion and cold-start install time.
evidence: apps/mobile/assets/icon.png present as binary blob in diff
apps/mobile/assets/splash.png present as binary blob in diff
apps/mobile/assets/adaptive-icon.png present as binary blob in diff
No evidence of @expo/image-utils or build-time optimization in the workflow
findings.suggested_fix: Replace placeholders with optimized branded assets (WebP or compressed PNG) and add an asset optimization step to CI, or document maximum asset dimensions for designers.

findings.title: NativeWind className strings are resolved at runtime increasing bundle and startup cost
findings.why_it_matters: NativeWind's Babel output transforms className at runtime. For an MVP this is acceptable, but as the design system grows the runtime style computation and bundled CSS parser add measurable JS thread work on lower-end Android devices.
evidence: All UI components use className strings extensively
findings.suggested_fix: For future iterations consider compiling NativeWind at build time or migrating performance-critical lists to StyleSheet-based primitives. Not blocking for MVP.

residual_risks: The network probe fires every 30 seconds plus on every foreground event. On a fleet of internal-test devices this is negligible, but at scale it adds background load to the Convex deployment and should be measured.
ConvexReactClient keeps a persistent WebSocket open. On Android with aggressive Doze mode, repeated reconnects may drain battery if not tuned.
testing_gaps: No benchmark or load test proving mobileOverview stays within Convex function document-read limits.
No render-count test for AuthProvider consumers to catch context-value instability.
No bundle-size budget or CI check for the mobile app binary.
